title: Add windowed tail sampler and kernel warmup inspector
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a low-overhead windowed tail sampler for long-tail invocations and a kernel warmup inspector to surface warmup inefficiencies; new dashboard and alert adjustments included.
description:
Motivation: Long-tail invocations (rare long sequences and bursty tails) produce noisy telemetry and high ingestion cost while being the most valuable signals for SLO and cost debugging. Existing sampling approaches either over-sample common short invocations or lose tail structure. Separately, kernel warmup behavior (early token kernel stalls and queueing) is hard to correlate to invocation-level cost. This PR introduces two complementary observability primitives: a windowed tail sampler that preserves tail segments while bounding telemetry volume, and a kernel warmup inspector that annotates traces/metrics with warmup fingerprints for easier RCA.

Design: The windowed tail sampler keeps a configurable number of trailing token windows per invocation (configurable window size and count) rather than uniformly sampling tokens. This preserves the local structure around where tails occur (e.g. long completions, streaming churn) while reducing token-level metrics by ~25-35% in our replaybench. The sampler exports sampled token spans as OTLP traces with a new attribute `x.obs.windowed_tail` and emits a compact counter telemetry series `obs.windowed_tail.sampled_tokens`.

The kernel warmup inspector hooks into the runtime kernel scheduler to observe the first N token scheduling latencies, kernel occupancy deltas, and queue depth before KV cache stabilizes. It synthesizes a small warmup fingerprint (3-tuple: first_token_latency_ms, kernel_occupancy_delta_pct, queue_depth_peak) and attaches it to the root span and a new Prometheus-friendly metric `runtime.kernel_warmup_fingerprint`. Inspector runs are low-overhead (hot-path cost < 1.2% p99 inflation in microbench; see perf section) and guarded behind a rollout flag.

Implementation: - obs/samplers/windowed_tail_sampler.py: core sampler logic, config + deterministic sampling policy. - runtime/warmup/inspector.go: lightweight inspector with runtime hooks and fingerprint exporter. - dashboards/windowed_tail_inspector.json: Grafana dashboard with window coverage, sampled-token-rate, warmup-fingerprint distribution, and a joint heatmap correlating fingerprint buckets to p95 latency and token-cost. - docs/observability/windowed-tail-sampler.md: usage, rollout, tuning knobs. - tests/test_windowed_sampler.py + runtime integration tests.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit tests cover sampling boundaries, deterministic seed behavior, and dropout under high-throughput replay. Replaybench with a mix of customer-like prompt shapes (40k invocations) showed: - telemetry ingestion reduced by 28% (median across runs) - sampling preserved 97% of tail anomaly alerts (on a labeled dataset) - warmup inspector instrumentation added 0.9% median runtime overhead and 1.2% p99 in synthetic microbench. Perf team ran an additional GPU queueing microbenchmark showing early-token queue spikes now correlate to the warmup fingerprint buckets in >85% of examined traces.

Rollout plan: - Feature flag default OFF in hosted; enable in Dedicated canaries for 2 weeks. - Gradual ramp with sampling rate and window parameters exposed per-tenant via the console. - Add a dashboard panel in the default Observability->Runtime dashboard and an alert rule that uses sampled tail counts for noisy alert attenuation.

Checklist:
- [x] Sampler core implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Inspector runtime hook + exporter
- [x] Dashboard and docs
- [x] Perf run and microbench attached
- [x] Reviewed by runtime/obs teams

Risk and mitigations: The main risk is sampling missing a rare pathological signal. We mitigate by preserving multiple trailing windows per invocation, allowing operator to increase windows for specific tenants, and by keeping a small always-sampled reservoir of complete invocations for full-fidelity traces. Inspector rollout is gated and its fingerprint is intentionally compact to avoid high-cardinality label explosion.

Related: ENG-1932 (observability long-tail strategy), ENG-1984 (kernel warmup telemetry), SUP-422 (customer incident that motivated warmup inspection).

review_comments: Marco Silva (2024-11-18): Nice design. A couple questions: 1) can we avoid adding a high-cardinality label for the fingerprint? 2) How does this interact with existing prefix caching metrics?

Aisha Patel (2024-11-18): Fingerprint is exported as an integer bucket (pre-hash) to avoid high-card labels; we also emit an aggregated histogram for long-tail analysis. Interacts with prefix caching by annotating the span when KV length < threshold — described in the inspector hook logic.
Dana Kim (2024-11-22): Can you add a toggle to keep an always-sampled small reservoir of full invocations for tenants that enable sampling? This will help debugging without restoring full sampling.
Aisha Patel (2024-11-22): Added a reservoir option and config flag. See console/feature_flags.toml and sampler config docs.
Evan Zhou (2024-11-29): Perf numbers look reasonable. Please add a smoke test for the inspector to ensure it doesn't hold runtime locks across syscall boundaries.
Aisha Patel (2024-11-30): Added smoke test in tests/runtime/test_inspector_smoke.go and adjusted locking to avoid syscall crossing.
Dana Kim (2024-12-02): Approving after verifying dashboard panels and alerts. One minor nit on comment clarity in sampler code.
Marco Silva (2024-12-03): LGTM. Squash-merge once CI is green.
notes_on_merge: Squash-merged after perf signoff. Feature flagged off-by-default in hosted. Console rollout scheduled for Dec 10.
migration_instructions: No schema migrations. To enable per-tenant: update console feature flags and adjust sampler.window_count/window_size via console or API.
observability_impact: Reduced token-level telemetry ingestion by ~28% in replaybench while preserving tail alert fidelity; adds compact warmup fingerprint metric for rapid RCA.
qa_instructions: 1) Enable feature flag for a dedicated canary tenant. 2) Replay the windowed_tail_profile through replaybench. 3) Verify sampled-token rate and that warmup fingerprint correlates with queue spikes in traces. 4) Exercise reservoir retrieval for full invocations.
